purpose: Expected gate outcome of the stage-1 card 'Where this program touches SAP standard' for the shipped starter examples, written down BEFORE lib/standard-touch.ts was run on them (docs/design/fit-to-standard-concept.md section 3.4; owner decision 22.10.2026). A case where the gate disagrees is a finding to report, not a knob to tune: change an entry here only with the reason in 'note'.
basis: Read from the source of each example against the classes of the concept, section 3.2 and 3.3: A deviation from a standard process (enhancement, BAdI implementation, modification); B own view on standard data (no writes, reads of SAP tables with a released path); C code driving standard transactions or BAPIs; D hard-coded customising (an add-on to A-C, never offered alone). Exclusions: no SAP object; integration as the main effect (outbound RFC, ABAP proxy, file exchange) with no A or C signal; own persistence as the main effect (writes only to its own tables) with no A signal.

Z_SALES_ORDER_CREATOR.txt.why: Creates sales orders through BAPI_SALESORDER_CREATEFROMDAT2; no own tables.

Z_INVOICE_EXTRACTOR.txt.why: Reads billing documents and writes a file on the application server for another system: an interface.

Z_MATERIAL_STOCK_CALC.txt.why: A read-only list over stock tables.

Z_MM_PO_APPROVAL.abap.why: Drives ME21N by batch input and calls BAPI_PO_CREATE1; also writes EBAN directly.

Z_SD_DELIVERY_PRIORITY.abap.why: A BAdI implementation that fills a field when a sales order is saved.

Z_SD_FREIGHT_RATE_CHECK.abap.why: Its main effect is the quote of an external carrier system over an outbound RFC, logged in its own table.

ZLEGACY_ORDER_FULFILLMENT_AUDIT_1000LOC..why: Changes sales orders through batch input on VA02, beside an outbound RFC and its own tables.
